extracted.intended_audience: USPTO primary examiners and CRU staff preparing examiner's answers in inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_short: examiner's answer for inter partes reexam
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required content for preparing an examiner's answer in an inter partes reexamination appeal, including required sections, procedural timing, and how to explain/rebut rejections and determinations of patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness of examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should furnish each party with a comprehensive examiner's answer that provides a written statement in answer to each appellant brief and each respondent brief, containing a response to the allegations or arguments made in all of the briefs and calling attention to any errors in an appellant's copy of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May incorporate from any of the briefs the most accurate and comprehensive information. If a ground of rejection or reason for patentability is not addressed, the proceeding will be remanded by the Board. An answer should include rebuttal of any and all arguments presented in all of the briefs. An examiner should reevaluate positions in light of briefs and expressly withdraw rejections or determinations not adhered to (but reopening prosecution is required if a new ground or new finding is made).

rubrics_metrics.name: Real Party in Interest statement
rubrics_metrics.description: For each appellant and respondent brief, the examiner must acknowledge the identification by name of the real party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate form paragraph(s) to identify which brief(s) contain the real party in interest. If no identification is contained, it is presumed the party named in the caption is the real party in interest, though the Board may later require an explicit statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Related Appeals and Interferences
rubrics_metrics.description: State and identify by application, patent, appeal, or interference number all other prior and pending appeals, interferences, or judicial proceedings known to the examiner which may be related to or have a bearing on the Board's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include copies of any court or Board decisions for proceedings identified under this paragraph in the Related Proceedings Appendix section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of whether the examiner agrees or disagrees with the statement of the status of claims contained in the briefs; if disagreeing, set forth a correct statement of the status of all claims in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is disagreement, explain the area of disagreement and include a correct statement (use form paragraphs referenced). Remember a 'final rejection' is not made in reexamination—use 'Action Closing Prosecution' and 'Right of Appeal Notice' terminology where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of Amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of whether the examiner agrees or disagrees with the statement of the status of amendments contained in any of the briefs, including amendments after Action Closing Prosecution (ACP); if there are no amendments, so state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific form paragraphs for: agreement, disagreement (explain reasons), amendment entered (include date), amendment not entered (include date), or that no amendment after ACP has been filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of Claimed Subject Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of whether the examiner agrees or disagrees with the summary of claimed subject matter contained in the briefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the summary is deficient, explain the deficiency and include a correct summary of the invention if necessary for clear understanding of the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of whether the examiner agrees or disagrees with the statement of the grounds of rejection to be reviewed set forth in the briefs and an explanation of any disagreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the subheadings 'Grounds of Rejection Not On Review' (listing grounds not withdrawn and not presented by appellant) and 'Non-Appealable Issues' (listing any non-appealable issues). Use 'None' where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings of Patentability to be Reviewed on Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of whether the examiner agrees or disagrees with the statement of the findings of patentability to be reviewed set forth in the briefs and an explanation of any disagreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the subheadings 'Findings of Patentability Not On Review' and 'Non-Appealable Issues' (and state 'None' where appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Appendix accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of whether the copy of the appealed claims contained in the appendix to the appellant briefs is correct, and if any claim is not correct, a copy of the correct claim must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow form paragraphs for indicating correctness or providing corrected claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence Relied Upon
rubrics_metrics.description: A listing of the evidence relied on (e.g., patents, publications, Official Notice, admitted prior art), and for non-patent references, the relevant page or pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that new references cannot be applied in an examiner's answer (37 CFR 41.69(b)); if new references are to be applied, prosecution must be reopened. Both art relied upon by the examiner and art relied upon by the third party requester must be listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, the examiner's answer must explain how the first paragraph is not complied with, including how the specification and drawings do not describe the subject matter defined by each rejected claim or would not enable a person skilled in the art to make and use the subject matter without undue experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include consideration of undue experimentation factors set forth in MPEP § 2164.01(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, the examiner's answer must explain how the claims do not particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which applicant regards as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific explanation tied to claim language and what is deficient in definiteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102 (anticipation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102, the examiner's answer must explain why the rejected claims are anticipated or not patentable under 35 U.S.C. 102, pointing out where all of the specific limitations recited in the rejected claims are found in the prior art relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to specific locations in the prior art showing each claimed limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 (obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103, the examiner's answer must (a) state the ground of rejection and point out where each of the specific limitations recited in the rejected claims is found in the prior art relied on, (b) identify the differences between the rejected claims and the prior art relied on (the primary reference), and (c) explain why it would have been obvious at the time of the invention to modify the primary reference to arrive at the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the proposed rejection is based on a combination of references, explain the rationale for not making the combination (when maintaining patentability) or, if making a rejection, explain why the combination would have been obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature-by-feature comparison when correspondence unclear (102/103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there are questions as to how limitations in the claims correspond to features in the art even after complying with the requirements for 102 and 103 explanations, the examiner must compare at least one of the rejected claims feature-by-feature with the art relied upon in the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comparison should align the language of the claim side-by-side with a reference to the specific page/column/line number/drawing reference number and quotations from the reference as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of other rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection other than those under 35 U.S.C. 112, 102, or 103, the examiner's answer must specifically explain the basis for the particular rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, specific factual and legal basis for any maintained rejection not covered by the enumerated categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinations of Patentability — general explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each determination of patentability (i.e., each determination of inapplicability of a proposed rejection), provide a clear explanation of the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must address proposed-for-rejection claims and explain why they are not rejected; mirror the structure required for grounds of rejection (e.g., explain compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112 first paragraph, identify which limitations are not found in the art for 102/103, and explain rationale where combinations are involved).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of inapplicability for 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: For each determination that a proposed-for-rejection claim is not unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. 112 first paragraph, the examiner's answer must explain how the first paragraph is complied with, including how the specification and drawings describe the subject matter and would enable a person skilled in the art without undue experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address enablement and written description with reference to specification/disclosure and undue experimentation factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of inapplicability for 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: For each determination that a proposed-for-rejection claim is not unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. 112 second paragraph, the examiner's answer must explain how the claims do particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain claim language and how it meets definiteness requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of inapplicability for 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103
rubrics_metrics.description: For each determination that a proposed-for-rejection claim is not unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103, the examiner's answer must explain why the proposed-for-rejection claims are not anticipated (102) or are patentable over the art relied upon (103), pointing out which limitations are not found and identifying differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the proposed rejection is based on a combination, explain the rationale for not making the combination; where correspondence is unclear, do a feature-by-feature comparison as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: No New Ground of Rejection or New Finding of Patentability statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's answer must provide an explicit statement that it does not contain any new ground of rejection and does not contain any new finding of patentability (i.e., no new determination of inapplicability of a proposed rejection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement reminds the examiner that if a new ground or finding is made, prosecution must be reopened, and notifies the parties appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to Argument
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of whether the examiner disagrees with each of the contentions of appellants and respondents in their briefs with respect to the issues presented, and an explanation of the reasons for disagreement with any such contentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any ground of rejection or inapplicability is not argued and responded to by the appropriate party, the examiner must point out each claim affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Proceedings Appendix (copies of decisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include copies of any decisions rendered by a court or the Board in any proceeding identified by the examiner in the Related Appeals and Interferences section of the answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach decisions in the Related Proceedings Appendix using the specified form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period for Providing a Rebuttal Brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner will set forth the period for the appropriate appellant party/parties to file a rebuttal brief after the examiner's answer and that no further papers will be permitted subsequent to the rebuttal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the exact time period and explicitly state the limitation on further submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing timing, signatures, and initialing
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner's answer is complete, the examiner will sign it; each conferee present at the appeal conference will place initials below the examiner's signature; the examiner must prepare and forward the case to CRU SPE/TC QAS no later than two weeks from the appeal conference (unless authorized otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clerical staff will copy the answer for patent owner and requester(s) and attach form PTOL-2070 for mailing to third party requesters. The CRU SPE/TC QAS reviews the answer and forwards to the RLA within three days of receipt; the examiner obtains conferee initials (initialing does not necessarily indicate concurrence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure approved amendments have been entered before preparing answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Before preparing an examiner's answer, the examiner should make certain that all amendments approved for entry have in fact been physically entered by the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The clerk of the Board will return any reexamination proceeding in which approved amendments have not been entered; confirm entry before finalizing the answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on including new references in examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner's answer may not include a new ground of rejection or apply new references in the answer; if new references are to be applied, prosecution must be reopened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 41.69(b) prohibits new grounds in the answer; to apply new references, reopen prosecution via an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of affidavits and declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should report conclusions on any affidavits, declarations, or exhibits admitted to the record, and clearly identify affidavits/declarations as being considered under either 37 CFR 1.131 or 37 CFR 41.154(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The distinction matters because the Board will usually consider holdings on 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits/declarations but not holdings on 37 CFR 41.154(a) affidavits/declarations in appeal cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when examiner's answer contains new legal interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner's answer is believed to contain a new interpretation or application of existing patent law, the answer, case file, and an explanatory memorandum should be forwarded to the CRU Director for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If approved by the CRU Director, forward the answer to the RLA for final approval prior to mailing the examiner's answer.
